summary: Asked whether few are saved, Jesus urges His hearers to strive to enter the narrow door, sends a reply to Herod, and laments over Jerusalem.
key_insight: Those shut out will say, “We ate and drank in Your presence, and You taught in our streets.” They had been near Jesus, yet He answers, “I do not know you, where you are from.” Being near Him is not the same as being known by Him.
story: Jesus went through the towns and villages, teaching as He journeyed toward Jerusalem. Someone asked Him, “Lord, are there few who are saved?”

Jesus answered them all, “Strive to enter through the narrow gate, for many, I say to you, will seek to enter and will not be able.” Once the Master of the house had risen and shut the door, those outside would knock and say, “Lord, Lord, open for us,” and He would answer, “I do not know you, where you are from.”

Then they would protest, “We ate and drank in Your presence, and You taught in our streets.” But He would say, “I tell you I do not know you, where you are from. Depart from Me, all you workers of iniquity.” There would be weeping and gnashing of teeth when they saw Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, and themselves thrust out. People would come from east and west, from north and south, and sit down in the kingdom of God. “And indeed there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.”

That same day some Pharisees came and said, “Get out and depart from here, for Herod wants to kill You.” Jesus answered, “Go, tell that fox, ‘Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.’ ” He would keep on His journey, “for it cannot be that a prophet should perish outside of Jerusalem.”

Then He cried out, “O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the one who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, but you were not willing!” Their house was left to them desolate, and they would not see Him until they said, “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the LORD!”

scene.label: Few or many?
scene.text: Jewish teachers debated how many would share in the age to come. Some held that all Israel would; the writer of 2 Esdras, late in the first century, lamented that many are created but few will be saved. Jesus gives no number. He answers a question about others with a command to the one who asked.

scene.label: The door
scene.text: The NKJV says “narrow gate,” but Luke’s word is the ordinary word for a house door, the same door the Master shuts in the next verse. At a feast, once the host shut the door, latecomers stayed outside.

scene.label: That fox
scene.text: Herod Antipas ruled Galilee and Perea, so Jesus was in his territory. Foxes were known as sly and destructive (Song of Solomon 2:15; Ezekiel 13:4). Luke does not say whether these Pharisees meant to protect Jesus or simply to move Him on.

scene.label: Under her wings
scene.text: Scripture often pictures God sheltering His people under His wings (Psalm 91:4; Ruth 2:12). Jesus speaks of Jerusalem’s children as One who had longed, many times, to give them that shelter.

scene.label: A pilgrim psalm
scene.text: “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the LORD” is Psalm 118:26, from the Hallel, the psalms sung at the great pilgrim feasts. Crowds will shout a form of it as Jesus rides down the Mount of Olives into Jerusalem (Luke 19:38).

witnesses.luke: Only Luke records the question about the few, the warning about Herod and Jesus’ reply. He reminds readers that Jesus was “journeying toward Jerusalem” (13:22), and the passage ends with the city itself, where a prophet must die. Matthew records almost the same lament in the temple during the last week (Matthew 23:37–39); Jesus may well have spoken it twice, first on the road and then within the city walls.

seeing.reveals: Jesus walks toward the city that kills prophets, unhurried by Herod’s threat, because His “third day” is set by God, not by a fox. And He grieves over the people who will refuse Him, longing to gather them like a hen gathers her brood.
seeing.living: Do not rest on having been near Jesus, at His table or under His teaching. Strive to enter now, through the door He opens, while it stands open. Let Him gather you as He longed to gather Jerusalem.
seeing.ponder: Does Jesus know you, or have you only been near Him?

preaching.big_idea: The door is narrow and will not stay open; being near Jesus is not being known by Him.
outline: A door that will be shut (24–30)
A prophet who will not be turned aside (31–33)
A Savior who longed to gather (34–35)
preaching.watch_for: The question “are there few who are saved?” gets no number. Jesus answers with “Strive” (v. 24) and then a reversal: some who were close are shut out, while people from every direction sit down in the kingdom (vv. 28–30).
